findings.summary: New. A row identifies its warning by WarningPath {index, depth} into WarningEngine.warnings, not by reference. Because each click opens another form (tool_windows.rs:377), a second form that removes or adds a warning shifts the indices. The first form's rows then edit, or with '-' remove, a different warning. In C# they keep editing their own (possibly detached) object. The combo popup ids are salted only with (index, depth), so open forms share popup state.
findings.required_fix: Hold a shared handle to the CustomWarning (for example Arc<Mutex<CustomWarning>> in WarningEngine.warnings and Child), and implement Remove/removewarning by pointer identity. Salt egui ids with the form instance as well.

findings.cs_reference: Warnings/WarningControl.cs:96-160 (ComboBox default DropDownStyle.DropDown, FormattingEnabled; SelectedIndexChanged fires on an index change, not on text)
findings.summary: New. The three combos are non-editable egui ComboBoxes. In C# they are editable DropDown boxes: typing sets Text without SelectedIndexChanged, and setting Text to a value not in the list moves SelectedIndex to -1 and raises the event. The port compares text instead of index, so re-selecting after a typed value, or Text set to an unlisted name, behaves differently. NUM_warning/NUM_repeattime reuse SimpleGrid's numeric_updown, which still lacks the wheel and key behaviour (R73-33).
findings.required_fix: Port ComboBox DropDown semantics (an editable text with an index model and SelectedIndexChanged on index change) as a shared control, and use it here and in SimpleGrid.

findings.summary: New. check_ctor only peeks at the cell. In C# the protected constructor reads Instance, which runs SingletonCreator's static constructor first. So the first stand-alone 'new T()' creates the singleton (whose inner Instance read sees null) and then throws 'You have tried to create a new singleton...'. If the creator stored an exception, Instance rethrows it from the constructor. The port accepts the first stand-alone construction and ignores a stored exception.
findings.required_fix: In check_ctor, call Instance() when the cell is empty and not being initialised by this thread (track re-entrancy), and return the stored exception if there is one.

verdict: Build passes with 0 warnings and tests pass (487 passed, 1 ignored), but 'cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets' now fails: 18 deny-level approx_constant errors on MercatorProjectionGCJ's PI literal stop mp-core, so mp-app is not linted. Ported lines rose to 45,801 / 479,014 (9.6%, 198 files), which raises the cap to 2.0. The ports are careful. The Warning Manager is a real copy of WarningsManager/WarningControl down to the designer's overlapping labels and the constructor's event order. The GCJ and polar projections, Stuff (verified against real GMap ciphertexts), StringUtils/ColorUtils/LoadSave and an exact System.Random are literal. Three claimed fixes are confirmed: NUL bytes, NaN projection keys and GPointComparer. However, about 5,400 of the 6,044 new lines have no caller, the Warning Manager's rows reference warnings by index rather than identity, QuickPanel Coloring is now offered but does nothing, and the STATUSTEXT path still lacks the compid copy. The screenshots show a recognisable Mission Planner skin but not an exact one: egui window chrome, egui::Modal dimming and fade on every dialog, a FlightData panel that grows from 300 to 425 px, a different Messages time format, client areas about 19 px short, and widespread text clipping. Several capture cases do not show their subject. Awarded 1.6 of a 2.0 cap. Round-file fidelity 6.9, UI/UX 2.9, features 3.8, visual 4.5.
